## Tickets

### POLISH-009: Refusals carry codes and details; the web app says what to change

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-29. Every server refusal now carries the IDs it concerns
only in `details`, never in `message` (`invalid_request` names each field's
path and Zod code in `details.fields`); a scan that fails at commit names its
root only in the status's `rootId`. The web app words `invalid_request` by
field and Zod code in `http/refusal-words.ts`, every reservation refusal in
`channels/specials/special-words.ts`, a show already on the lineup in Add
shows, and a failed runtime stop in the My Channels cleanup notice; an
overlap names the other Special by its airtime, since a Special has no
title. Route tests assert through `testing/refusal-details.ts` that each
changed sender's message holds no ID and its details do. Deferred: the
reservation preview's `channel_unschedulable` sender has no route test. Its
message is a fixed string with `channelId` in details, and it is reachable
with an explicit-end collection Special on an empty collection on a channel
with no shows.

**Goal**: No `✖`, no `→ at`, no database ID, and no "reservation" reaches
the owner.

**Scope**: Server: `sendInvalidRequest` puts each Zod issue's path and code in
`details.fields` and a plain message; `sendChannelNotFound`, the reservation
refusals, and any other `message` that interpolates an ID move the ID to
`details`. Web: `apps/web/src/http/refusal-words.ts` maps `invalid_request`
by field name and Zod issue code to one sentence per field it knows;
`channels/specials/special-words.ts` maps every `ReservationRefusal["kind"]`,
naming the other Special by its airtime from details. `RequestFeedback` shows the mapped
sentence when a mapping exists, else the message.

**Out of scope**: Renaming any code; changing HTTP statuses.

**Blocking dependencies**: None.

**Implementation notes**: Follow `removal-messages.ts`. The route coverage
tests already list every refusal; extend them rather than adding a suite.

**Verification**: Server: a test per changed sender asserts the message has no
ID and details carry it; web: one test per mapped code. `grep -rn "✖"
apps/web/src` finds nothing.

**Docs impact**: Spec 0006 and 0007 refusal tables, if they quote messages.

### POLISH-010: Availability label and file names in every list

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-29. `media-availability/availability-label.ts`, a
top-level folder because four web domains read it, names each status
Available, Missing, or Could not be read for the library column, the Filter,
the scan summary, the Special media picker, and every collection row, which
now shows the file name (the full path on hover); the status route also counts
unreadable members, so the strip says "1 could not be read". There was no link
color on `.secondary.path-cell` to drop.

**Goal**: `probe_failed` never appears on a screen; rows are scannable.

**Scope**: `apps/web/src/media-library/availability-label.ts` returns
Available, Missing, Could not be read; the library's Availability column, the
picker rows, and the member rows use it, omitting Available in rows. Picker
and member rows show `fileName(path)`; the full path stays in Details. The
filter dialog reads its labels from the same function.

**Out of scope**: Changing the status values or the filter semantics.

**Blocking dependencies**: None.

**Implementation notes**: Drop the link color from `.secondary.path-cell`.

**Verification**: jsdom tests render each status through all three lists.

**Docs impact**: None.

### POLISH-011: The collection status says what can air and why not

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-29. The status route counts missing and
too-short members in its one pass, the web contract mirrors them, and the
editor strip reads "Nothing to air yet, add media below." or "N of M can air
(1 missing, 1 too short)" from `collections/collection-words.ts`; the Live
Monitor's schedule-gap advice names the same causes. A member whose probe
failed is counted in neither cause, so its collection reads "0 of 1 can air"
with no reason; a "could not be read" count is a follow-up.

**Goal**: An owner whose clip is too short learns that, in the collection.

**Scope**: The status route adds `missingCount` and `tooShortCount` beside
`schedulableCount`; the web contract mirrors them; `collection-editor.tsx`
renders "Nothing to air yet, add media below." or "N of M can air (…)" with
the reasons present. `airing-words.ts` gains the same cause for the Live
Monitor's "Nothing is scheduled" advice.

**Out of scope**: Changing the duration floor.

**Blocking dependencies**: None.

**Implementation notes**: The route already filters members for
schedulability; count the two reasons in the same pass. Mirror the contract
in `apps/web/src/http/contracts/` and extend the recorded cross-package-copy
exception if the audit reports the pair.

**Verification**: Route test with one missing and one short member; jsdom
test for the sentence.

**Docs impact**: GLOSSARY "Schedulable" unchanged; spec 0002 (automatic
collections) status strip line, if it quotes the old text.

### POLISH-012: Scan summary in match-review words

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-29. The scan dialog's completion summary lists Files
found, Could not be read, and Missing, then the match states in the words
`match-state-label.ts` exports: Matched, Needs your choice, Unmatched, and
Lookup failed. The Probed row and the "n need your choice." sentence are
dropped as repeats of rows. Spec 0002's list was amended to those words
because spec 0001 and the glossary already own the match review's labels;
spec 0009's and spec 0001's summary paraphrases are historical and stand.

**Goal**: The first scan's completion reads as a result, not a pipeline.

**Scope**: The eight summary labels in `scan-progress-dialog.tsx` become
Files found, Could not be read, Missing, Matched, Needs your choice,
Unmatched, Lookup failed, drawn from `match-state-label.ts` where a state
exists.

**Out of scope**: Changing the counts the server reports.

**Blocking dependencies**: None.

**Verification**: Existing scan-progress jsdom suite updated for the words.

**Docs impact**: Spec 0009 (background scans) summary table, if it quotes
labels.

### POLISH-013: Preview lines in owner words

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-29. `preview-words.ts` words each turn as time, show, and
what plays in the show's content unit, says "already airing", "normal
rotation" only while a rule is in play, and "marathon" with its stretch and no
chance; skips name the show and the reason, and the lists are **Upcoming
shows** and **Skipped shows**. `countWords` and `minutesWords` are exported
from `stretch-words.ts` for reuse rather than copied.

**Goal**: The Preview tab answers "did my channel work?" in plain words.

**Scope**: `upcoming-programming.tsx` renders each line as time, show, what
plays ("9:54 PM · Bluey · 1 episode (7 min)"); skips name the show and the
reason; "normal rotation" appears only when a rule is active; marathon lines
say "marathon" and the stretch without percentages or rounds.

**Out of scope**: The preview data itself.

**Blocking dependencies**: None.

**Implementation notes**: Put the sentence builders in
`channels/preview/preview-words.ts` so the jsdom test can cover every branch
without rendering.

**Verification**: Unit tests over `preview-words.ts` for program, skip, rule,
and marathon lines; grep for "assignment" in the file finds nothing
user-visible.

**Docs impact**: Spec 0008 preview section wording, if it quotes lines.

### POLISH-014: Plex Setup copy

Complete on 2026-10-29. Step one reads "Create a channel and add at least one

**Scope**: Separate "set" from `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` with an explicit space; step

fix-it box reuses the wrong-address screen's sentence about `-e` in Docker.

**Out of scope**: Address detection (ADR 0019).

**Blocking dependencies**: None.

**Docs impact**: None.
